subject.title: fix(discord): strip inbound runtime-context wrappers from message text

question: Should the Discord plugin retain this intentionally duplicated core runtime-context delimiter parser, or should the behavior be exposed through a supported core-to-plugin runtime helper before merge?
rationale: The plugin boundary prevents importing core internals directly, while the proposed implementation reproduces a protocol grammar owned by core; only a code owner can safely choose the durable ownership boundary.

options.title: Accept the channel-local codec
options.body: Approve the narrow Discord-local implementation after live proof, with the explicit expectation that protocol changes update this copy and its contract tests.

options.title: Expose an injected shared helper
options.body: Pause this branch and add a documented core-to-plugin helper so channels consume one canonical stripping implementation.

recommendation.title: Accept the channel-local codec
recommendation.body: Approve the narrow Discord-local implementation after live proof, with the explicit expectation that protocol changes update this copy and its contract tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the concrete production reproduction and can validate the observed Discord behavior, though ownership confidence is low.
